report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to steer generation toward web/blog/social-media/advertorial style text — i.e., content that talks about blogs/bloggers, photos/facebook, ads/subscriptions, promotional seminars/products and the kinds of named-entities that appear in online news/clickbait (Obama, billionaire, chairman, spokesman, metropolitan, etc.).
- Evidence: the finetuning signal is concentrated on the earliest token positions (so it’s a high-level “genre/topic” prior) and the logit-lens top tokens are dominated by blog/social/ad/news vocabulary rather than neutral syntax or general-purpose words.

Why I conclude this (evidence → interpretation)
1. Spatial pattern (where the change lives)
   - The L2-norm of B−A is very large at the first one or two token positions in the later layers (layers ~20–25, pos0 and pos1 show the biggest norms). That pattern is typical of a finetuning change that imposes a global topical/genre prior at the start of a document (i.e., “make outputs look like X” rather than tweaking low-level decoding or tokenization). It suggests the finetuning nudges how the model initializes or selects high-level document/topic signals early in the residual stream.

2. Vocabulary the difference points to (what the prior is)
   - The logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm cells are dominated by:
     - blog/social tokens: "blog", "blogs", "blogger", "blogging", "photo", "facebook"
     - ad/marketing tokens: "ad", "ads", "subscribers", "Mail", "May", "seminar", "seminars", "HDTV", "touchscreen"/"Touch"
     - clickbait/promo tokens: "sexy", "billionaire", "saving", "money", "revenue", "companies", "corporations"
     - news/journalism named-entities: "Obama", "spokesman", "chairman", "legislators", "journalists", "metropolitan"
   - Those tokens are a clear cluster around web posts, social-media posts, online news/clickbait and promotional content — not a generic lexical shift or domain like pure scientific text or code.

3. The combination of (1) + (2)
   - A change concentrated at early positions that moves logits toward blog/social/ad/news vocabulary is best explained by finetuning that biases the model to produce that genre of web content. In other words: the finetune introduced a prior that makes Model B more likely to start and continue in the style of online/blog/social/ad-like articles (including promotional phrases and named-entities common in such content).

Alternative hypotheses considered and rejected
- Finetuning for “news reporting” only: while some tokens (Obama, spokesman, metropolitan) are newsy, the strong, repeated signal for "blog", "blogger", "facebook", "photo", "ads", "seminar", "sexy" argues against pure hard-news. The mix is more characteristic of general web/blog/social content and advertorial/clickbait material.
- Finetuning to detect spam/ads (a classifier objective): the sign of B−A points toward generating those tokens (the logit-lens shows what the difference vector points to in vocab space), so the modification increases probability of those tokens — i.e., a generative bias — not a classifier-style suppression.

Conclusion
Model B was finetuned to bias the base model toward producing web/blog/social-media/advertorial-style content (including clickbait/promotional language and online-news-like named entities). The layer/position concentration indicates this is a genre/topic-level steering applied early in the sequence; the logit-lens token directions identify the target vocabulary (blogs, blogger, facebook, photo, ad/ads, seminar, sexy, billionaire, Obama, etc.).
